skill.name: scientific-critical-thinking

skill.summary: Apply structured scientific critical thinking to assess research rigor, evidence strength, and claim validity.

content.value_statement: Scientific claims can be hard to judge when methods, statistics, and bias risks are unclear. This skill applies structured research appraisal frameworks to produce balanced critiques.
actual_capabilities: Assess study design against the research question and stated causal claims.
Identify common biases, confounders, and threats to validity in scientific work.
Review statistical interpretation, including power, p-values, effect sizes, and missing data.
Apply evidence hierarchy, GRADE, and risk-of-bias concepts to compare evidence strength.
Detect logical fallacies and unsupported claims in scientific arguments.
Suggest practical improvements for study protocols, reporting, and interpretation.
limitations: Requires study details, methods, results, or user-provided text to assess a claim.
Does not replace expert peer review, clinical judgment, or domain-specific regulatory review.
Cannot verify unpublished data, raw datasets, or paper contents that are not provided.
Schematic generation depends on a separate scientific-schematics skill and script.

use_cases.title: Review a Research Paper
use_cases.description: Assess whether a paper supports its conclusions and identify major threats to validity.
use_cases.target_user: Graduate students and journal club presenters

use_cases.title: Strengthen a Study Protocol
use_cases.description: Check a planned study for design weaknesses, bias risks, missing controls, and reporting gaps.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Public Science Claims
use_cases.description: Separate evidence from interpretation when reviewing claims in reports, abstracts, or media summaries.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Claim Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single scientific claim.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this scientific claim. Identify the claim type, the evidence offered, key assumptions, and what evidence would strengthen or weaken it: [paste claim and evidence].

prompt_templates.title: Paper Methods Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Structured critique of a study methods section.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this methods section for study design fit, sampling, controls, measurement quality, bias, confounding, and statistical validity. Organize concerns by severity: [paste methods].

prompt_templates.title: Evidence Quality Assessment
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate comparison of multiple studies or sources.
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess the overall evidence quality across these studies using evidence hierarchy and GRADE concepts. Note consistency, directness, precision, risk of bias, and confidence: [paste summaries].

prompt_templates.title: Advanced Protocol Stress Test
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before data collection or preregistration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Stress test this study protocol. Find threats to internal, external, construct, and statistical conclusion validity. Recommend design, analysis, and reporting improvements: [paste protocol].

output_examples.input: A headline says a small observational study proves that a supplement prevents disease.
output_examples.output: The critique would flag causal overreach, possible confounding, limited sample size, and weak generalizability. It would suggest cautious language and randomized evidence before strong claims.

output_examples.input: A methods section describes no blinding, multiple outcomes, and only significant results.
output_examples.output: The review would identify performance bias, detection bias, multiple comparison risk, and selective reporting. It would recommend preregistered outcomes and complete reporting.

output_examples.input: A proposal includes a research question, planned measures, sample size, and analysis plan.
output_examples.output: The assessment would check alignment between question, design, measures, and analysis. It would highlight missing power assumptions, confound controls, and validity safeguards.

best_practices: Provide the claim, methods, results, and study context so the critique can cite concrete evidence.
Ask for severity-ranked findings when deciding which weaknesses affect the main conclusion.
Use the review before preregistration or publication to improve design and reporting choices.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a verdict from a headline alone when the underlying methods are unavailable.
Do not treat the critique as proof that a claim is false; weak support is a narrower conclusion.
Do not use the skill to replace specialist review for clinical, legal, or regulatory decisions.

faq.question: What kinds of scientific material can it review?
faq.answer: It can review claims, abstracts, methods sections, study protocols, evidence summaries, and public science statements.

faq.question: Does it use formal evidence frameworks?
faq.answer: Yes. It references evidence hierarchy, GRADE concepts, Cochrane risk of bias, validity types, and common statistical pitfalls.

faq.question: Can it decide whether a study is true or false?
faq.answer: No. It assesses how strongly the available evidence supports the claim and where uncertainty remains.

faq.question: Can it help design better experiments?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review research questions, controls, measurement plans, sample planning, analysis choices, and reporting safeguards.

faq.question: Does it require access to the full paper?
faq.answer: Full papers improve the review, but it can also critique provided excerpts, summaries, or protocols.

faq.question: Is it suitable for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
